mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 2.5% over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, which drives negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate below 5% for two consecutive months indicates a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing corporate profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly negative at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1 growth below 1% q/q for two consecutive quarters) signals weakening demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 q/q growth < 1% for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not significantly below zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for three consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces earnings for industrial firms and drags down S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly negative at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a monetary tightening accompanied by rising inflation, which increases real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both above 12-month moving average
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly below zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in both PAYEMS and UNRATE above their 12-month moving averages indicates a robust labor market expansion, which initially boosts consumer spending but eventually leads to higher wage inflation and margin compression, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as markets anticipate earnings growth before margin effects dominate.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and UNRATE both above 12-month moving average
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly above zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related earnings and consumer confidence, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 12-month moving average for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly above zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in Real Personal Savings (RSAFS) below its 12-month moving average for three consecutive months signals reduced household savings and higher consumption financed by debt, which temporarily boosts demand but increases financial risk and ultimately leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as deleveraging pressures emerge.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS < 12-month moving average for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly below zero at 5% significance.
